text.p: Flooding returns to Vietnam due to Tropical Storm Willie... Tropical Storm Willie is making landfall over northern Vietnam at this time. Top winds are near 55 mph but will rapidly drop off as the storm center moves over land during the next several hours. Heavy rain, with amounts of 4-8 inches and locally higher, will result in moderate to severe flooding with property and crop damage. Heavy rainfall may progress westward to Thailand by Tuesday where local flooding may occur.

Typhoon Violet is now centered over 200 miles northeast of Tokyo, Japan, moving rapidly to the northeast at 30 mph. Violet has top wind near 85 mph but will steadily weaken this period as it moves rapidly northeastward into the open northwestern Pacific. Violet will become extratropical within 24 hours. Some large ocean swells will continue along the east coast of Japan through the next 24-36 hours, though the main threat from this system will be to shipping from high winds and seas.
THERE ARE NO FURTHER EMERGENCY WEATHER STATEMENTS
